title: 8-bit weight sanity matrix and calibration orchestration
creator: Marina Lopez
description: Integrate INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ) quantization profiles into our CI regression harness and formalize a calibration orchestration playbook that covers numeric accuracy, sequence-length sensitivity, and runtime telemetry. The goal is a reproducible nightly validation matrix and a deterministic canary path for production rollouts.
background: We have multiple internal ad-hoc tests for weight-only INT8 quantization, but results across models and sequence lengths are noisy. New AWQ variants and hybrid GPTQ recipes are landing in the model catalog; we need a standard matrix that validates accuracy, latency, and token-quality regressions before any canary or release. Current gaps: coverage across seq-len buckets, cross-batch KV cache effects, embed/perplexity metric consistency, and automated fallback thresholds.
proposal:
1) Create a canonical 'sanity matrix' that runs GPTQ and AWQ profiles across 3 model shapes (base, L/XL), 4 sequence-length buckets (64/256/1024/2048), and two batch patterns (single-stream vs burst).
2) Orchestrate calibration pipelines that: collect calibration snapshots, run post-quant evals against golden prompt sets, compute delta metrics (R1 token-level exact-match, perplexity ratio, embedding cosine), and publish to our console dashboard.
3) Add regression gates in CI: fail-on-large-delta with per-model tolerances and advisory warnings for borderline cases.
4) Add a canary rollout playbook that exercises runtime fallbacks: model-variant fallback, region fallback, and auto-rollback on sustained metric regressions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sanity matrix job in CI that runs nightly and produces a matrix artifact (csv + json-summary) for all target models and seq-lens.
- Calibration orchestration that stores calibration snapshots to s3://redwood-quant-calibration/{date}/{model}/{profile} and links artifacts in the job logs.
- Console dashboard with a time-series for: token-delta, perplexity-ratio, embedding-cosine, median latency.
- CI gates: PR checks that run a fast smoke sweep; nightly job that gates release branches if thresholds exceeded.
- Canary runbook documented with clear rollback triggers and playbook steps.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (this sprint):
- Define matrix dimensions and select canonical models (owners: M. Lopez, D. Patel).
- Implement runner that launches workloads via existing runtime test harness; add config for GPTQ vs AWQ variants.
- Store outputs and minimal artifacts (log, decoded outputs, embeddings) to the calibration bucket.
Phase 2:
- Build summarizer that computes delta metrics and writes JSON summary compatible with console ingestion.
- Wire nightly job in CI and hook alerting for threshold breaches.
Phase 3:
- Integrate into canary pipeline with rollout gating and rollback automation hooks.
Estimated work: 8 points. Individual PRs: runner impl, summarizer, dashboard ingestion, CI job, playbook doc.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for summarizer metric calculations (edge cases: empty outputs, tokenization mismatches).
- Synthetic stress suite: long prompts (up to 8k tokens via chunking) to validate sequence-length behavior.
- Golden prompt regression: 1.5k prompts covering instruction, conversational, code, and retrieval-style queries.
- Nightly matrix: run on small subset (smoke) for PRs; full matrix nightly.
- Canary validation: run end-to-end traffic shadowing with opt-in customers prior to release.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: numeric drift due to randomness in GPTQ/AWQ calibration. Mitigation: use fixed seeds, snapshot calibration artifacts, and run multiple seeds for critical models.
- Risk: latency regressions from per-token quant overhead. Mitigation: include latency budgets in matrix and add perf telemetry hooks.
- Risk: false positives from tokenization differences. Mitigation: canonical tokenizer version per model recorded in artifact metadata.
notes: Decided to normalize perplexity deltas relative to FP16 baseline to account for model size differences. Use embedding cosine thresholds for semantic regression detection; set an initial advisory threshold at 0.98 for small models, 0.995 for L/XL as a conservative starting point.
